content.title: Josh Hokit added to UFC White House card after Donald Trump and Joe Rogan plead with Dana White
content.text: Photo by Jim WATSON / AFP via Getty Images UFC Sat 11 April 2026 23:31 Josh Hokit will fight on the UFC White House card after a request from Donald Trump.On Saturday, Josh Hokit capped off a memorable UFC 327 fight week with a blockbuster win over Curtis Blaydes to remain undefeated.The 28-year-old has stollen all the headlines this week due to his antics at media day when he attempted to spark an altercation with Jiri Prochazka, along with his performance at the press conference.His crazy antics and his incredible fight with Blaydes, though, have earned him a surprising spot on the UFC White House event this coming June. Was Blaydes vs Hokit the craziest heavyweight fight of all time?🤯🔥 Curtis Blaydes and Josh Hokit put on a spectacular show at UFC 327! Sum that fight up in the comments. Photo by Ed Mulholland/Zuffa LLC jamie.theodosiFeatured commentI was almost certain after the first 20 seconds that it wasn’t gonna go past the first round!1dynel3Featured commentDid not think it’d go past the 1stsfbluenileFeatured commentThe craziest heavyweight fight of all time came in Strikeforce…Hendo vs Fedor Dana White adds Josh Hokit vs Derrick Lewis to White House cardFollowing the fight, Joe Rogan asked on the Paramount broadcast whether it is too late to add ‘The Incredible Hok’ to the historic White House card.And Rogan’s prayers were answered as UFC boss Dana White was sat cageside with Donald Trump taking in the action in Miami.And following arguably the craziest fight of all time, Trump turned to White and asked him why popular heavyweight contender Derrick Lewis isn’t on the historic June 14 card.Photo by Ed Mulholland/Zuffa LLC“I’ve got one for you guys, I’m sure you guys just saw the Hokit fight, right?” White said during an Instagram live.“So about an hour ago, the president leaned over to me and said ‘why isn’t Derrick Lewis on the White House card’, and I said ‘hold on a second Mr President’.“I stepped away and called Derrick Lewis and said ‘Derrick, the President just asked me why you’re not on the card, do you wanna fight on the White House card?’ he said, ‘of course I do’.“Then the Hokit fight plays out and Joe Rogan says, is there still room on the White House card? I went back and talked to him, Hokit vs Derrick Lewis was just added to the White House card in the last 10 minutes. President Trump built half the fight, Joe Rogan built the other.“Both guys have accepted and agreed to fight so we’re adding one more to the White House. Pretty badass how that came together organically.”Join Our NewsletterReceive a digest of our best Bloody Elbow content each week direct to your mailbox Photo by Jeff Bottari/Zuffa LLCMMA Nate Diaz makes UFC dig by dubbing Netflix card with Rousey and Ngannou ‘best of the free fighters’ Wed 15 April 2026 20:00 Some of the sport’s biggest names were on stage for the latest press conference ahead of Netflix’s very first MMA event.The streaming giant will enter the mixed martial arts world on May 16 with a stacked card at Inglewood’s Intuit Dome, headlined by Ronda Rousey’s comeback against Gina Carano.Those two won’t be the only prominent names returning to the cage after layoffs. Joining them are former UFC heavyweight champion Francis Ngannou and fan favorite Nate Diaz.Those four appeared at Wednesday’s press conference alongside Mike Perry and Philipe Lins, where they continued to hype up the event and what it will mean for the current state of MMA.LATEST NEWS: Mike Perry reveals ‘incredible’ UFC fighter he’s training with to prepare for Nate Diaz on Netflix Nate Diaz or Mike Perry? Nate Diaz and Francis Ngannou share ‘free’ from the UFC sentiment at Netflix press conferenceThe event on May 16 is being promoted by Jake Paul’s Most Valuable Promotions, which put on Wednesday’s presser in New York City.Many have suggested the lineup is the best MVP could have put together given who is available outside of the UFC. Diaz seemingly shares that sentiment, having taken a dig at the UFC by calling the Netflix card the “best of the free” fighters during the recent presser.“It’s a big opportunity to be part of Netflix’s first MMA card—to be alongside these guys right here, the best of the best. The best of the free,” Diaz said.The Stockton star said that comment while sitting alongside Ngannou and Rousey, both of whom have been vocal in criticizing UFC pay and contracts in recent times.‘The Predator’ was asked about Diaz’s description by host Ariel Helwani, and he expanded on it.“It’s the reality. Can you count how many fighters out there are free and can be in this spot?” Ngannou said.“This is the opportunity so many fighters would like to have, but which of them would be able to take it? Maybe they are stuck in a contract that most don’t like,” he added.LATEST NEWS: Ronda Rousey uses Jon Jones double standard to reject concern over her making MMA comeback aged 39Netflix’s Ronda Rousey vs Gina Carano card has lost one fightWhile anticipation is high for the event on May 16, the card has not avoided the injury curse.Among the intriguing undercard matchups was a clash between ex-UFC star Lorenz Larkin and former Bellator welterweight champion Jason Jackson.But the Rousey vs Carano card took a hit recently when Larkin announced his withdrawal due to an injury.“I’m sorry to all the fans but I had to pull out [of] the Netflix card due to [a] knee injury,” Larkin wrote on his Instagram Story. “[I] will be rehabbing it back to 100% and will be back.”A potential replacement opponent has yet to be announced for Jackson, who has not competed since being released by the PFL.Join Our NewsletterReceive a digest of our best Bloody Elbow content each week direct to your mailbox Photo by Brandon Magnus/Zuffa LLC/Zuffa LLC via Getty ImagesUFC Conor McGregor publicly thanks Artem Lobov after settling $6.5 million lawsuit over Proper No. 12 Wed 15 April 2026 17:30 UFC star Conor McGregor can now put his full focus back on a return to the Octagon after the conclusion of Artem Lobov’s lawsuit.The former lightweight and featherweight champion has been inactive since 2021, when McGregor broke his leg against Dustin Poirier at UFC 264.He’s had his eyes on ventures away from the cage but is planning to change that this year, targeting a long-awaited UFC comeback in the summer.And when it comes to dialing in on another fight, the Irishman has eliminated one distraction.LATEST NEWS: Joe Rogan questions one aspect of Nate Diaz vs Mike Perry: ‘Wonder why they agreed on that?’ CHANGE MY MIND: Conor McGregor is the UFC’s greatest legend 'Notorious' took MMA to the next level at the height of his legendary career. Conor McGregor settles with Artem Lobov after being sued over Proper No. 12Former UFC fighter Artem Lobov rose to fame as a teammate of McGregor’s during his journey to multi-weight success in the promotion. Their relationship is far from what it once was, and the pair have even been battling one another on the legal front in recent years.Lobov and McGregor’s feud went public when ‘The Russian Hammer’ sued ‘The Notorious’, claiming a stake in his Proper No. Twelve Irish Whiskey. Lobov took credit for McGregor’s brand, insisting he came up with the idea and provided key ideas and research on the matter. The Russian admitted he had turned down McGregor’s $1 million offer after the company’s success, alleging that he’d been promised five percent “no matter what” by his ex-teammate.Lobov sued for that share, which would have amounted to $6.5 million of the $130 million reportedly taken home by the UFC star when McGregor sold Proper No. Twelve for $600 million.The case was due to commence on Wednesday in the High Court and was scheduled to last eight days. However, Lobov’s attorney Andrew Walker told the judge that a settlement had been reached and a trial was no longer required.“I want to thank him for his hard work for my whiskey business,” McGregor said in a statement after the settlement (h/t Irish Independent).The Russian opted not to issue a statement after the settlement, details of which were not disclosed.LATEST NEWS: Ronda Rousey uses Jon Jones double standard to reject concern over her making MMA comeback aged 39Photo by Brandon Magnus/Zuffa LLC/Zuffa LLC via Getty ImagesMcGregor’s attorney Mark Lyman read his statement to the court, which included a comment about how the ex-UFC champ is now looking forward to focusing on his training for “this summer’s fight.”His UFC return is not yet confirmed but is reportedly slated to headline International Fight Week in July, with Max Holloway the frontrunner to welcome him back to action.Join Our NewsletterReceive a digest of our best Bloody Elbow content each week direct to your mailbox Photo by Julio Aguilar/Getty ImagesUFC Mike Perry reveals ‘incredible’ UFC fighter he’s training with to prepare for Nate Diaz on Netflix Wed 15 April 2026 17:00 Mike Perry is getting work in with an electrifying UFC lightweight ahead of his return to mixed martial arts.Perry will be among the top names competing on the card for Netflix’s very first MMA event on May 16.Before Ronda Rousey headlines against Gina Carano, Perry will face Nate Diaz as both men make their MMA comebacks after a number of years away.Many who predict a victory for Diaz envision ‘Platinum’ being submitted, and Perry has revealed who he’s training with to hopefully stop that from happening.LATEST NEWS: Joe Rogan questions one aspect of Nate Diaz vs Mike Perry: ‘Wonder why they agreed on that?’ Nate Diaz or Mike Perry? Mike Perry is training with UFC fighter Terrance McKinney ahead of his MMA return against Nate DiazFor Perry, the five-round welterweight clash at Inglewood’s Intuit Dome will mark his first time competing in MMA since a loss to Daniel Rodriguez spelled the end of his UFC tenure in 2021.Since then, the 34-year-old has fought exclusively in striking-only realms, becoming a star in the Bare Knuckle Fighting Championship and also sharing the ring with Jake Paul in boxing.With that in mind, Perry admitted that getting back into MMA training has been somewhat of a shell shock during a recent appearance on The Ariel Helwani Show.Fortunately, ‘Platinum’ has a prominent UFC star helping him gear up for the Diaz showdown.“It’s been tough,” Perry said.“I’ve been doing really good on diet and taking care of my body, stretching, ice tubs, getting chiropractic work.“The grappling aspect, I get to work with really great fighters at Fusion X-Cel in Ocoee, Florida,” he continued. “I’ve been working a lot with Terrance McKinney. He’s an incredible athlete, an incredible fighter.“He goes for broke, but then in the gym, he’s so calculated, and he’s such a good wrestler and grappler. It’s been great working with Terrance. His MMA skills are fantastic.”LATEST NEWS: Ronda Rousey uses Jon Jones double standard to reject concern over her making MMA comeback aged 39Copyright 2021 Getty ImagesMcKinney knocked out Kyle Nelson in just 24 seconds at UFC Seattle last month.The lightweight fighter now has 17 first-round finishes in 18 professional wins in mixed martial arts, with eight coming in the UFC Octagon.Fans will see if his habit of fast starts has rubbed off on Perry in training when he shares the cage with Diaz on May 16.Join Our NewsletterReceive a digest of our best Bloody Elbow content each week direct to your mailbox
